newsitem.title: TURKEY: ISUZU'S TURKEY VENTURE SEES HIGHER 1997 SALES.
newsitem.headline: ISUZU'S TURKEY VENTURE SEES HIGHER 1997 SALES.

text.p: Turkish commercial vehicle maker Anadolu-Isuzu, partly owned by Japan's Isuzu Motors Ltd and Itochu Corp, targets sales to rise to 20 trillion lira this year from 9.4 trillion in 1996, its general manager Kamil Eser said.
The company set its export target at $9 million after $4 million last year, Eser told Reuters.
Anadolu-Isuzu's major export destinations are the Middle East and countries from the former Soviet Union.

The company, listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange in April, produced 2,381 vehicles in the first five months of 1997, up from 1,975 in the same 1996 period. It targets production of 5,200 vehicles -- 5,000 trucks and 200 busses, over the year as a whole Eser said.

He said the company would use proceeds of a public offering in April -- worth 1.8 trillion lira -- to finance a $5.5 million modernisation project and establishment of a new production plant near the north-western town of Gebze.
The company will produce 11,000 vehicles a year at the Gebze plan after the $38-million plant becomes fully operational by mid-1999.
